### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

_No response_

Hope this can be done as a bugfix.. realy would like to get started with the Energy Dashboard.

Did some more digging in the code... and this might need more work then I though first.
Also I noticed another problem with the YouLess integration (#55605) which might be related.

The class ExtraMeterSensor is used for both the total and usage which both need different units of measurements and both need a different state_class (while the class currently even lacks the state)

In my local environment I experimented a little by copying the component into a custom_component.
Editing the class ExtraMeterSensor into the following seems to work for my environment.

`class ExtraMeterSensor(YoulessBaseSensor):
    """The Youless extra meter value sensor (s0)."""

    _attr_native_unit_of_measurement = ENERGY_KILO_WATT_HOUR
    _attr_device_class = DEVICE_CLASS_ENERGY
    _attr_state_class = STATE_CLASS_TOTAL_INCREASING

    def __init__(
        self, coordinator: DataUpdateCoordinator, device: str, dev_type: str
    ) -> None:
        """Instantiate an extra meter sensor."""
        super().__init__(
            coordinator, device, "extra", "Extra meter", f"extra_{dev_type}"
        )
        self._type = dev_type
        self._attr_name = f"Extra {dev_type}"
        
        if dev_type is "usage":
            self._attr_native_unit_of_measurement = POWER_WATT
        if dev_type is "usage":        
            self._attr_device_class = DEVICE_CLASS_POWER
        if dev_type is "usage":
            self._attr_state_class = STATE_CLASS_MEASUREMENT        
`

With this I am able to use Extra total for my Energy dashboard.
Also this fixes my problem with the Extra usage (#55605)

I hope a more experienced Python and Home Assistant developer is able to fix these issues in a correct way
Issue is still present in Release 2021.9.1 - September 2

@walterbressers that is to be expected as this ticket is still open and no commits or pull-requests are related. In other words no work has yet been done to fix this.

@reharmsen just to verify and get things correct. You are not receiving the solar through the delivery sensors? These should be read from the P1 of the power meter? The extra sensor should not be needed for this. It might also be related to #55646 if a change in the extra sensor is required. It will require the sensor model in the integration to be reworked, adding a switch like that is not preferred as the two sensors have different responsibilities.

@gjong 
I noticed two 'issues' 

1) 
I was not able to use the 'Extra total' in the Energy Dashboard.
this is most probably due to missing of attr_state_class = STATE_CLASS_TOTAL_INCREASING 
and perhaps also due to the fact this sensor has _attr_device_class = DEVICE_CLASS_POWER

This is reported in this (#55535) issues, and also seems to be reported by @sweebee in #55646

2)
I also use the Power wheel card (see HACS), to display Energy usage in my house. (might going to replace with the native Energy dashboard)

This card complained that 'Extra Usage' did not have the correct unit of measurement.
The card expects W, as I also use power_usage (which is in W).
This is most probably due to _attr_native_unit_of_measurement = ENERGY_KILO_WATT_HOUR
I reported this originally in #55605 (which now is closed)


In both issues I do have the data read from the YouLess.. and they also get into Home Assistant in the "Extra total" and "Extra usage" sensors, but I am not able to use this information correctly as the mentioned attributed are not filled or incorrect.


As for how I use my YouLess:
I use the P1 port to read my utility meter (gas, power_delivery and power), next to this I use the S0 (extra) port for a kWh meter which registers my solar output.. This allows for calculating the exact amount of energy used by our house 


As I mentioned yesterday with the supplied code.. it works for me (since just before the post) with these edit's.
But I can imagine it's not the most elegant solution to manipulate the attributes like this.. and might not get past code review.
